title: What "your file never leaves your device" does and does not cover
description: A precise account of the privacy claim: what never happens, what is still fetched from the network, and how to verify it yourself.
seoTitle: File Privacy: What Stays on Your Device
seoDescription: A precise breakdown of the browser-side privacy claim: which network requests never happen, which page and engine requests still occur, and how to check.

body.text: "Your files are never uploaded" is a strong claim, and strong claims deserve a precise reading. Here is exactly what it covers, what it does not, and how you can check the second one yourself.

body.caption: Your file has one path. The code that touches it has several.

body.text: When you add a file, it is read into the memory of your browser tab and processed there. The result is produced there and handed back to you as a download. At no point does a request carrying your file leave the page — there is no upload endpoint on this site to send it to.

This describes the reviewed public-tool implementation. It has no selected-file upload workflow. The claim does not cover private files you decide to attach to an email or submit to another service. Browser extensions, a compromised device or a changed deployment can also affect what runs in a page.
What still happens over the network
The page and processing code still require network requests. Your selected file is not part of those requests:

items: Interface fonts come from your device. Page HTML, styles, JavaScript and editorial images are requested from this site; no external font service is used.

Processing engines are downloaded from this site on first use — the FFmpeg WebAssembly build for media, the image encoder for photographs. Those are program files, served from this origin, and they are code rather than data.

body.text: In the tab, as memory buffers, and as temporary object URLs that make downloads possible. Queue entries retain their input and result while you review them. Removing an entry, clearing results or closing the tab releases application references; the browser decides when to reclaim the memory.

The application does not persist selected tool files in localStorage, IndexedDB, the Cache API or cookies. The browser can cache website resources and engine code. A download you save is a separate file on your device and remains there until you remove it. Releasing a queue entry is not a secure-erasure guarantee.

body.title: The consequence worth knowing
body.text: The application has no server copy from which to restore your selected file. A crash or closed tab can lose an unsaved result, while your original stays in its device location. Keep that original and save any result you need before clearing the queue.

Open your browser’s Network panel, clear its list and process a generated file. Inspect actual request URLs and payloads. The expected application requests fetch page resources and engines rather than submitting the selected file. Extensions and unrelated tabs can create their own traffic; distinguish those from this page instead of treating every request as a file upload.

That is the difference between a privacy policy and a privacy architecture. A policy tells you what someone promises not to do. The reviewed application avoids transferring selected files. That does not protect against a compromised browser, extension or hosting environment.
Page requests, support and editor sessions

Cloudflare still handles ordinary website requests and may process connection and security data. Automatic analytics/RUM is disabled for the public site. Support email and the authenticated TinaCMS editor have separate service providers and data handling; neither is required to process a file in a public tool. Read the [Privacy Policy](/privacy) for these distinctions, or use the [contact page](/contact) for a question without sending private files.
